note.backdrop: Friday's half session closed higher: the S&P 500 fund +1.62%, the Nasdaq 100 fund +2.69% and small caps +1.83% against Wednesday's close. For the holiday week the Nasdaq 100 fund gained about 7.0% and the S&P 500 fund about 5.6%; CNBC said the S&P 500 was headed for its best week since April 2025 (StockTitan). The Nasdaq 100 fund closed at $650.99, a cent or so below Monday's $651.03, so it won back nearly all of Tuesday's and Wednesday's fall. Gold futures closed +3.75% and the 10-year yield rose to 4.94% from 4.85% (Yahoo closes read by the engine). After the 1 p.m. close the market was quiet (k: S&P 500 fund +0.4%, futures flat), and the five stocks flagged outside their ranges each rest on one or two after-hours prices (the engine's trade counter from 1 p.m. ET: Revvity 1, Yum China 1, SLM 1, Restaurant Brands 1, Mettler-Toledo 2), so they are stray prints on a holiday afternoon, not news. Markets reopen on Monday for a full session.

themes.beneath: The week in one line: Monday's 31% jump on the chief executive's return, two days of selling AI hardware and its builders, and a Friday that put the index back where Monday left it. Reported: the closes. My inference, as at midday: the market treats Nvidia's two open matters (S&P Global Ratings' watch over how it is governed, and Friday's report that barred chips were installed in Shanghai) as Nvidia's own, separate from demand for AI hardware, which the memory makers' gains say is still strong. Gold and the 10-year yield rose on the same day as stocks (+3.75%, +0.09 point), so it was not a rally on falling rates or on fear going away from bonds; the cause of gold's move is still not found.
themes.cause: The broad rise of the morning held: the Nasdaq 100 fund ended almost exactly at Monday's close and the S&P 500 fund above it (StockTitan, k). Chips led to the end: SanDisk +15.96%, Micron +7.60% (to $646.95), AMD +4.56%, Broadcom +3.82%. Nvidia closed +0.80% at $150.49 (StockTitan; Yahoo closes).
themes.mechanism: Measured from Wednesday's close, the rest of the chip trade won back its whole two-day fall; Nvidia won back about 8% of its own ($150.49 against $149.30 Wednesday and $165.05 Monday; StockTitan).
themes.name: The rebound holds to the close; Nvidia sits it out
themes.watch: Monday's full session: whether the week's gains hold; Nvidia against $149.30 and $165.05; any word on the chips in Shanghai or on Nvidia's credit rating.
